questions: Can the edge reversal operation be performed multiple times, and if so, does each reversal toggle the direction of all edges (i.e., flipping them back and forth) or does it set them to a fixed reversed orientation regardless of previous reversals?
Is the edge reversal operation allowed at any time, including when at vertex N (though the process stops upon reaching N), or only when not at N?
If multiple edges exist from the current vertex, can we choose any one to move along, and is there any restriction on revisiting vertices or edges?
Does the cost X for reversing edges apply per reversal, and is it fixed regardless of how many edges are reversed?
Is the goal to minimize the total cost to reach vertex N, or is it to compute the cost of a specific predetermined sequence of operations?
Are self-loops (edges where u_i = v_i) allowed, and if so, can moving along them keep you at the same vertex?
Does the reversal operation affect all edges globally and instantaneously, or only edges in a specific subset (like incident to current vertex)?
Is there any limit on the number of operations (moves or reversals) that can be performed, or can we continue indefinitely as long as we haven't reached N?
